note: Single machine-readable source of truth for every public technical claim about citrate-chain. Each value is tied to source files and, where applicable, reproducible evidence. Website and marketing facts MUST be generated from this file, not hand-copied. Numbers here were measured/derived from the code at source_commit; see verification_status per claim. See verification/README.md for status definitions.

salt_total_supply.unit: whole SALT (base tokens; multiply by 10^decimals for wei)
salt_total_supply.notes: Code comment: scaled 1000x from a former 1B cap at the 2026-09 reroll. TOTAL_SUPPLY is the single source of truth; TokenConfig::default and GenesisConfig::validate derive the wei cap from it. Any 1-billion figure on public surfaces is stale.

chain_id.notes: Testnet and mainnet configs both pin 40204. 40204 == 0x9d0c.

ghostdag_k.notes: GhostDAG blue-set anticone bound k = 18, consumed by core/consensus/src/ghostdag.rs via GhostDagParams.

block_time.reproduction_command: grep -n 'block_time\|target_block_time' node/config/testnet.toml  # config target=1s. Live: sample consecutive block timestamps via RPC (eth_getBlockByNumber) and diff them -> ~1.9-2.0s.
block_time.notes: DISCREPANCY: config target_block_time = 1s (testnet.toml:7,40), but the LIVE measured block interval is ~1.9-2.0s (call it ~2s). Public surfaces should quote the measured ~2s, not the 1s config target. The config comment also records a whitepaper 500ms aspiration. (Legacy testnet-config.toml at repo root uses block_time=2, consistent with the measured value.)

checkpoint_interval.notes: [checkpoint] interval=50, committee_size=100, quorum_threshold=67 (2/3+1 BFT committee finality, WP-W.2). These are CONFIGURED parameters of a mechanism that is specified but NOT running: no production code path calls CheckpointManager::propose, so no checkpoint is ever proposed or finalized (see deterministic_checkpoint_finality).

deterministic_checkpoint_finality.reproduction_command: python3 verification/check_claims.py  # fails if this claim says running=true while no non-test code path calls .propose(
deterministic_checkpoint_finality.notes: Checkpoint finality is SPECIFIED, NOT RUNNING on the public testnet: CheckpointManager is constructed, but no production code path calls propose(), so no checkpoint is finalized. Confirmation is probabilistic. The RPC does not serve the 'finalized' block tag. Do NOT publish a finality time (the old 90-100s figure assumed a running committee).

confirmation_latency.notes: Confirmation is probabilistic: a block lands every ~2s (measured) and gains weight as later blocks build on it. Checkpoint finality is specified, not running. 'depth >= 100' is a display heuristic used by the explorer, not a protocol guarantee. No end-to-end measured latency artifact is published yet.

foundry_tests.count_method: forge test --use 0.8.36 final summary line ('2913 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped')
foundry_tests.notes: Measured on forge 1.5.1-stable at 3c256a59 (the commits since change no Solidity). 158 test suites, 2913 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.

rust_tests.count_method: cargo test --workspace -- --list | grep -c ': test' (each ': test' line is one #[test]/#[tokio::test] case). The per-binary 'N tests' summary lines sum to the same 4379, cross-checking the count.
rust_tests.notes: 4379 unit/integration test cases across the workspace, measured at 3c256a59; later commits change only a doc comment and one test assertion, so the count is unchanged (whole workspace compiled clean, exit 0). Doctests are NOT included (cargo --list does not enumerate them). Marketing surfaces have quoted 5,377 and 6,720 Rust tests; DO NOT copy those; 4379 is the measured figure. (Static grep of #[test]/#[tokio::test] annotations gives ~4,696, an upper-ish approximation that miscounts cfg-gated/macro-generated cases.)

deployed_contracts.reproduction_command: python3 verification/check_address_code.py --check  # read-only eth_getCode on every book entry; --offline validates the committed snapshot without network
deployed_contracts.count_method: Entries in contracts (69) + aaStack (7) = 76 book entries. eth_getCode at the probed block: 57 have code, 19 are codeless (not deployed). genesis.ArachnidDeterministicDeployer (1) and two top-level entries (CitrateMemberSBT, MembershipStakeVault) are tracked separately and have code. Precompiles (21) are codeless by design.
deployed_contracts.notes: The public number is 57 contracts with code on chain 40204, NOT 76. The 19 codeless book entries (the governance and cooperative set: AnchorRegistry, MeetingRegistry, GovernanceTemplateRegistry, GovernanceProtocolFactory, PolicyBinding, CapabilityGrant, VoteAllowance, Sortition, PatronageLedger, ModelCooperative, FacilitySBTImpl, NetworkSBTImpl, FacilitySBT, NetworkSBT, CitrateCooperativeFactory, CoopDeployer, CoopMembershipSBT, ContributionRewardPool, CoopGovernor) are NOT deployed; a value transfer to one of them succeeds and strands the value. The book (deployedAt 2026-09-12) is the canonical table; never hand-copy addresses into READMEs.

precompiles.notes: Canonical scheme (WP-B0): the EVM address IS the documented short name. ModelDeploy=0x0100, ModelInference=0x0101 per the dispatcher and 40204.json. FLAG: contracts/src/ModelRegistry.sol:17-18 hardcodes MODEL_PRECOMPILE=0x...1000 and ARTIFACT_PRECOMPILE=0x...1002, which DISAGREE with the canonical inference family (0x0100-0x0106). ModelRegistry's precompile calls therefore target 0x1000/0x1002, addresses outside the pure-precompile set and not present in 40204.json. Tracked as a discrepancy to reconcile.

model_registry_precompile_flag.notes: DISAGREEMENT CONFIRMED. ModelRegistry.sol calls address 0x1000 (=4096) / 0x1002, but the canonical model precompiles live at 0x0100/0x0101. 0x1000 is not a registered pure precompile in the dispatcher nor in 40204.json's precompiles table.

current_testnet_sustained_tps.derivation: block_gas_limit(30,000,000) / gas_per_simple_transfer(21,000) / measured_block_time(~2s) ~= 714, rounded to ~750 for simple transfers
current_testnet_sustained_tps.reproduction_command: grep -n 'MAX_GAS_PER_BLOCK' core/sequencer/src/mempool.rs; python3 -c 'print(30_000_000/21000/2)'  # ~714; tools/citrate-bench can confirm the live figure once bench signers are funded (signs client-side via eth_sendRawTransaction)
current_testnet_sustained_tps.notes: Peak is gas-limit bound: there is NO 10,000 TPS headroom on the current testnet. A block holds at most 30M/21k = ~1428 simple transfers, and blocks land ~every 2s, so sustained simple-transfer throughput is ~750 TPS.

mainnet_target_sustained_tps.notes: Aspirational mainnet target. Requires raising the block gas limit AND faster blocks (a consensus/protocol change). NOT yet implemented; owner decided NOT to change consensus params now.

mainnet_target_ceiling_tps.notes: Aspirational mainnet ceiling, same protocol-upgrade dependency as the sustained target.

executor_parallel_ceiling.notes: SEPARATE, HIGHER metric: the executor's in-memory parallel-execution throughput (not end-to-end network TPS, which is RPC/signature/gas-limit bound and far lower). In-process microbench via core/execution/benches/tps_parallel.rs; no committed artifact yet.

network_tps.notes: HONEST SPLIT (owner decision 2026-09-24). Public surfaces must distinguish: (1) current testnet ~750 TPS sustained for simple transfers, derived from the 30M block gas limit / 21k gas per transfer / ~2s block time and gas-limit bound (no 10k headroom); (2) mainnet targets of 5000 sustained / 10000 ceiling, which are target-pending-protocol-upgrade (require a higher gas limit + faster blocks, a consensus change not yet done); (3) the executor's in-memory parallel throughput, a separate and higher figure. The previously cited artifacts benchmarks/benchmark_2026_03_20.md and parallel_tps_verified_2026_04_21.md DO NOT EXIST; the old flat 5000/10000 'network baseline' has been replaced by this split. The deprecated tests/load benchmark_suite.rs must not be used for release claims; the canonical live harness is tools/citrate-bench.

tla_specs.reproduction_command: for r in citrate-chain nat nist-agent coop core citrate-memories citrate-comms citrate-explorer; do gh repo clone CitrateNetwork/$r; done && find . -name '*.tla' | wc -l
tla_specs.count_method: Clone the PUBLIC repos and run: find -name '*.tla' | wc -l. 102 specs today (chain 71 + nat 8 + nist-agent 6 + coop 4 + core 4 + memories 3 + comms 2 + explorer 2 + agentile 1 + cluster 1); the public-facing claim is '100+'.
tla_specs.notes: Public-facing count is '100+ TLA+ specifications across the public repositories' (102 today), publicly verifiable by cloning the public repos and running find -name '*.tla' | wc -l. The fuller authored corpus (~169 specs) lives in the PRIVATE internal archive (citrate-agentile-archive), which is NOT publicly countable; do not use 169 as a public claim. Marketing decks saying 121-122 are stale and should be regenerated from the public-countable 100+ figure.

transaction_signing_flow_states.reproduction_command: java -jar tla2tools.jar -config wallet/TransactionSigningFlow.cfg wallet/TransactionSigningFlow.tla  # spec lives in the private internal archive; re-run to reproduce the ~50B-state model-check
transaction_signing_flow_states.notes: Owner ran the full TLC model-check on TransactionSigningFlow to ~50 billion states. The spec is NOT in any public repository (there is no specs/tla/account/ in citrate-chain), so public surfaces must not present this as publicly reproducible; say 'owner-run on a private spec' or omit it. Reproducible from the spec, which lives in the PRIVATE internal archive (citrate-agentile-archive); the multi-TB traces from that run were NOT retained. The earlier 73M figure was a smaller/bounded run and is superseded.

evm_revm.notes: EVM execution via revm pinned to exact version =10 (default-features off; std + serde). Adapter in src/revm_adapter.rs.

consensus_ghostdag.notes: GhostDAG (Kaspa-family) blue-set consensus with k=18 and strict VRF proof checks (strict_vrf=true). Current topology: the public testnet runs a SINGLE block producer operated by Citrate (one producer address across a 51-block live sample on 2026-09-25; ValidatorRegistry activeSet() has 1 member). Stake-gated proposer eligibility is staged: OFF by default, enabled when CITRATE_VALIDATOR_REGISTRY is set (CITRATE_VALIDATOR_ACTIVATION_HEIGHT is optional and defaults to 0; node/src/main.rs:1443-1462). The BFT checkpoint committee (size 100, quorum 67) is the TARGET design and is not running. Any operator identity requirement is policy, not enforced by node or consensus code.

audit_status.notes: Classified Tier 1 (full external audit required before first stable v1.0.0 tag). No written external-firm audit attestation exists yet; internal adversarial re-audits and cargo-audit tripwires are in place. Prerelease tags may ship with a prerelease flag + warning.
